info.title: Time-Addressable Data Store
info.description:
The Time-Addressable Data Store (TADS) is used for storing timeline data.
The TADS consists of a service providing a database index of the Tracks and Track Events associated with them.
This document is a specification of the service API.

See the [bbc/tads](https://github.com/bbc/tads) repository for more background on TADS.

post.description:
Register to receive event notifications as webhooks on a specified URL.

Webhook messages will conform to the format in the `webhooks` section of the API docs, depending on the event type (as defined in the same section).

HTTP events sent by the service to a client webhook's endpoint SHOULD include a header with the header name given by `api_key_name` and the header value given by `api_key_value`.
Clients SHOULD verify this against the value they provided when registering the webhook.

Service Implementations MAY partially support event filtering and transformations.
Service Implementations SHALL return a 400 response code if the filtering or transformation specified in the request is not supported.

Service Implementations SHOULD consider the security implications of providing webhooks, and include appropriate mitigations against Server Side Request Forgery (SSRF) attacks and similar.
Service Implementations SHOULD take appropriate steps to authorize the modification of existing webhooks. This may take the form of RBAC, or ABAC.

201.description: Created. The webhook has been registered.

400.description: Bad request. Request body JSON is not valid or unsupported event filtering or transformation.

put.description:
Create or replace the Track metadata.

Clients should aim to populate as many of the Track metadata fields as possible and practical. The fewer parameters that are set, the higher the likelihood that reading clients will be unable to determine compatibility.

Some parameters may be ignored/overridden by Service Implementations. This is to enable the Track JSON-blob to be re-used with no/minimal editing in various use cases. Such parameters are called out in their description.

Track metadata can only be replaced/updated if:

* The Track property `read_only` is not 'true'
* The changes do not invalidate any Track Events owned by the Track
  * Note, determining the impact of Track metadata edits on all these Track Events could be a costly compute operation and so Service Implementations MAY choose to limit the Track metadata modifications that are permitted in certain scenarios.

get.description:
Return the list of Track Events owned by the Track.

Each Track Event attaches payload data to a specified timerange on the Track timeline.

The response body is an array of Track Events. This array MAY be empty.

Sorting of results:

* Track Events are sorted by `timerange`, in ascending order by default.
* When sorting in ascending order: Track Events are sorted using the start timestamp of the `timerange`.
* When sorting in descending order: Track Events are sorted by the end timestamp of the `timerange`.
* If multiple Track Events have the same sort order:
  * These Track Events are then sorted by the other timestamp of the `timerange`.
  * If multiple Track Events still have the same sort order:
    * These Track Events are then sorted by `id`.
* Service Implementations MUST take into account the inclusive/exclusive marker associated with a timestamp when it is used for sorting.

Pagination:

* Clients should use the pagination options to limit the results to a timerange and/or count.
* Service Implementations may also limit the results returned. This will be signalled via the paging headers in the response.

post.description:
Create or modify either a single Track Event or an array of Track Events.

Each Track Event attaches payload data to a specified timerange on the Track timeline.

Only permitted if the Track property `read_only` is not 'true'.

The request body must consist of either a single Track Event or an array of one or more Track Events.

Each Track Event in the request body MAY specify an `id` to identify the Track Event. For example, this could be used to edit Track Events or when transferring Tracks between Store Instances.

For each Track Event in the request body:

* If the Track Event does not specify an `id` then this is an instruction to create a new Track Event in the Store Instance. The Service Implementation MUST generate an `id` for the Track Event.
* If the Track Event specifies an `id`:
  * If a Track Event with this `id` already exists in the Store Instance then this is an instruction to replace it with the Track Event provided.
  * If a Track Event with this `id` does not exist in the Store Instance then this is an instruction to create a new Track Event with the specified `id`.

The Service Implementation SHOULD attempt to process all the Track Events in the request body regardless of any errors that might occur. That is, an error in processing one Track Event SHOULD NOT prevent the other Track Events from being processed.

A 200 response provides the results of processing the Track Events. Inside this response body, the `http_status_code` property MUST use the following values:

* `200`: Success. Track Event replaced/modified/updated.
  * This applies even if the values of the Track Event properties have not changed, in which case the Track Event can be considered "reaffirmed".
* `201`: Success. Track Event created.
* `400`: Error. The Track Event violates at least one constraint. Such constraints include:
  * The `id` of each Track Event MUST be unique within the Store Instance.
  * Each Track Event MUST belong to exactly one Track. As such, each Track Event attaches one `payload` to one `timerange` on one Track.
  * `payload` MUST validate against the Track's Payload Schema, identified by the `schema_id` property of the Track.
  * `timerange` MUST be valid according to the `timerange` definition and the relevant Track properties (such as `edit_rate` and `allow_overlaps`).
* `403`: Error. You do not have permission to carry out the creation/modification of this Track Event.

200.description: Return the list of Track Events responses.

400.description: Bad request. The request body JSON is not valid with respect to the specified JSON Schema.

403.description: Forbidden. You do not have permission to modify this Track. It could be marked read-only.

If Track Event deletion takes too long then this request will return 202 Accepted and the `Location` header will point to a Track Delete Request to monitor deletion progress.

parameters.name: sort_by
parameters.description:
Parameter to sort Track Delete Requests by.
`created` and `expiry` sort most recent first by default.
Sorting may be reversed using the `reverse_order` query parameter.
Assume `created` if not set.
For resources where the selected parameter is unset, `id` shall be used.
Resources using this fallback shall be sorted after those that aren't by default, and before when `reverse_order` is `true`.

get.description:
Return the list of Track Delete Requests.

A Track Delete Request is created when a client DELETEs a long timerange of Track Events, which takes longer than a single HTTP request.

Track Delete Requests currently being worked on are listed, for monitoring in development.

This will not necessarily list all requests, nor return a consistent set in any particular order, and should not be relied upon by clients. However if there are any requests in the system, it will always return at least one.

basic_auth.description:
HTTP basic authentication using a username and password.

This option should only be used in constrained cases where Bearer tokens are impractical, since the password is intrinsically long-lived, and managing user credentials across systems is difficult compared to using centralised auth (e.g. via OAuth2) with Bearer tokens

bearer_token_auth.description:
HTTP bearer token authentication.

The method through which a client should acquire a bearer token is assumed to be an OAuth2 grant (either the Authorization Code or Client Credentials grant), however the OpenAPI `OAuth Flow` object cannot be used because it requires that the relevant URLs are known in advance.

Clients should provide options to allow one (or both) grant types to be configured, as appropriate.

Where tokens are not JWTs, or are acquired through some other mechanism, the API key method should be used instead.

url_token_auth.name: access_token
url_token_auth.description:
URL token authentication.

The method through which a client should acquire the token is not specified: it is assumed this takes place in another way, and a TADS client may well be passed a URL to a TADS Service Instance including the token.

Clients should retain the token in the `access_token` query string parameter, and use it for subsequent requests to the TADS Service Instance in the same session.

timerange.title: TimeRange
timerange.description:
A timerange of timestamps. It is represented using one or two timestamps with inclusivity and exclusivity markers.

E.g.
* `[0:0_10:0)` represents 10 seconds of media starting at timestamp `0:0` and ending before `10:0`.
* `(5:0_` represents a timerange starting after `5:0` and to eternity.
* `_` without timestamps or inclusivity markers represents "eternity" (i.e. the entire timeline).
* `()` without timestamps represents "never" (i.e. a range of zero length in no particular position).
* `[1694429247:0_1694429248:0)` is a 1 second TAI timerange starting at 2023-09-11T10:46:50.0Z UTC.
* `[1694429247:0]` is an instantaneous TAI timerange at 2023-09-11T10:46:50.0Z UTC.
  This is equivalent to `[1694429247:0_1694429247:0]`.
  The short syntax is preferred due to ease of identification as instantaneous.
  Instantaneous TimeRanges cannot use exclusive markers (i.e. `(` or `)`).
* A `[` or `]` indicates that bound is inclusive, and a `(` or `)` indicates that bound is exclusive.

Details of the format can be found in the [Timestamps in TAMS](https://github.com/bbc/tams/blob/main/docs/appnotes/0008-timestamps-in-TAMS.md) application note.

If the metadata_version for Track instances is identical then the metadata is identical. Service Implementations SHOULD set suitable default values for `metadata_version` whenever Track metadata is changed and `metadata_version` is either not set by the client, or set to it's existing value. Service Implementations MAY permit clients to edit the value, subject to suitable permissions-based limitations. Where media is transferred between TADS Service Instances without changing the Track metadata, clients SHOULD maintain the `metadata_version`. To support this, Service Implementations SHOULD always accept the setting of `metadata_version` by the client on initial Track creation. Service Implementations SHOULD update this field where metadata is updated via child endpoints. Note that this specification places no requirements on incremental versioning. Service Implementations may, for example, choose to use hashes or date-time version identifiers.

Service Implementations MUST ensure that each Track Event in this Track has a `timerange` that meets this requirement.

More information about the error condition will be indicated by the Service Instance in the `error` parameter. Service Implementations SHOULD implement appropriate retries and only enter the `error` state when absolutely necessary. A webhook in the `error` or `disabled` state may be re-enabled by a client by setting the status to `created`. A webhook in the `created` or `started` state may be disabled by a client by setting the status to `disabled`. Attempting to transition an `error` status to `disabled` SHOULD be rejected.
